name: Wonderglen
lines: Lucky, and the critters love it.

A flower petal shaped like a little star.
From the Lily Pond. It glows softly in the dark.
From the Glow-worm Grotto. It twinkles, gently.

Pink icing and a sugar flower on top.

Made at the Craft Cottage. Give it to a friend, or keep it.

Glow shells that ring in the breeze.
A lantern you folded yourself.
Feathers for a tail, every colour of pebble paint.
Sparkle stones on a ribbon.

A soft toy foal with a silver horn.
It glows softly as it spins.
Twelve swirly marbles in a velvet bag.
Painted in stripes; it hums when it spins.
Blow bubbles anywhere you go.
Shake it: tiny petals swirl round a toadstool house.
A soft red nose that squeaks, just like the clowns' at the Big Top.

A tiny pink door in the roots of a willow. A note pinned to it says: "Gone to the Lily Pond. Back for tea."
A tiny blue door in a mossy stone, with a doorbell made from a bluebell.
A tiny yellow door under the hill, with a doormat that says WELCOME in very small letters.
A tiny green door in a tree stump, with a little window and a curtain that twitches.
A tiny violet door in the cliff, with a lantern no bigger than a thimble beside it.
The Bubble That Wanted to Stay
What did Bloop leave behind when it popped?
Moss the Shy Moonfoal
Why could Moss light the lantern when the others could not?
Moss's horn was small enough to fit
Moss ran the fastest
Moss had a box of matches
The Mushroom Who Forgot Its Note
How did Bellcap find its note again?
By listening to the notes on either side
By eating a cupcake
By asking the clouds
The Cloud Who Was Too Heavy
What made Nimbus light and fluffy again?
Sharing its rain with the thirsty flowers
Eating a honeydrop lolly
The Maze and the Brave Little Mouse
What trick did Juniper use to find the way?
Keeping one paw on the flowers and following them
Climbing over the walls
Flying with a balloon
What should you do if you find a fairy door?
Knock very softly once and say thank you
Shout as loud as you can
Try to open it with a key
Good zoos help look after animals that are rare in the wild. Some animals, like the Arabian oryx, were saved because zoos looked after them and then set them free again.
How can zoos help rare animals?
They look after them and set them free again
They teach them to fly
How a trapeze artist stays safe
Trapeze artists practise for years, start low down, and always have a safety net or a safety line. Catching a partner takes perfect timing: counting the swings together.
What keeps trapeze artists safe?
Practice and a safety net
Holding their breath

A soap bubble is a ball of air wrapped in a skin of soapy water thinner than a hair. Light bounces off the inside and the outside of that skin, and the two reflections mix into swirling rainbow colours.
What is inside a bubble?
Mushrooms are not plants
Mushrooms are fungi. They cannot make food from sunlight the way plants do, so they grow on old wood, leaves and soil and help turn them back into rich earth.
Mushrooms belong to which group of living things?
A lily pad floats because it is full of tiny pockets of air. Its roots are down in the mud at the bottom of the pond, joined to the pad by a long, bendy stem.
What helps a lily pad float?
Tiny pockets of air
Its roots pushing up
How old is a tree?
Every year a tree grows a new ring of wood under its bark. Count the rings on a stump and you know how many years the tree lived.
How can you tell how old a cut tree was?
Count the rings in the wood
Measure the shadow
A carousel spins round its middle. The beasts near the outside travel further on every turn than the ones near the middle, so they go faster, even though everyone goes round in the same time.
On a carousel, which riders go fastest?
The ones on the outside
The ones in the middle
They all go the same speed
What clouds are made of
A cloud is made of billions of tiny drops of water, or bits of ice, so small and light that they float in the air. When the drops join up and get heavy, they fall as rain.
What is a cloud made of?
Tiny drops of water or ice
In a maze whose walls are all joined together, if you keep one hand on the wall and never let go, you will always find the way out, though it may not be the shortest way.
What simple trick helps you solve many mazes?
Keep one hand on the wall
Always turn left twice
People told stories long before anyone could write. Stories were remembered and passed from grown-ups to children for hundreds and hundreds of years.
How did people share stories before writing?
By telling them out loud
By painting them on the moon
Red, yellow and blue paints are the primary colours. Mix yellow and blue and you get green; red and yellow make orange; red and blue make purple.
What do you get when you mix yellow and blue paint?
A rabbit's front teeth never stop growing! Chewing grass, hay and clover wears them down, so they stay just the right length.
Why do rabbits chew so much?
To keep their growing teeth the right length
Because they are bored
To sharpen their ears
The rainbow's order
A rainbow always has its colours in the same order: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. Some people remember it as the name Roy G. Biv.
Which colour is at the top of a rainbow?
Real glow-worms make their own light, called bioluminescence. Some glow-worms in caves hang sticky threads that shine like little stars to catch their dinner.
What do we call it when a living thing makes its own light?
Puzzles grow brains
When you solve a puzzle, your brain makes new links between its cells. The more puzzles you try, the better you get at spotting patterns.
What happens in your brain when you solve puzzles?
It makes new links
Letters and numbers
The English alphabet has 26 letters. Five of them, A, E, I, O and U, are called vowels.
How many letters are in the English alphabet?
the Welcome Pixie of the Kids Zone, small and quick, with lavender wings
Hello, hello! Welcome to Wonderglen, the Kids Zone of Faerie! Everything here is for playing. Would you like to know what there is to do?
the storyteller of Storybook Hollow, a very old and very kind fae with silver hair and a shawl of leaves
Come and sit, little one. The book is open and the story is ready.
the round, cheerful gnome who keeps the Honeydrop Tuckshop
Treats! Lovely treats! A few for everyone each day, and they cost nothing at all.
the keeper of the Lily Pond, in rubber boots, who watches the water so everyone stays safe
The pond's only shallow, dearie, but hop on the pads and you'll keep your socks dry!
the carousel operator, in a striped waistcoat, who knows every beast on the carousel by name
Step right up! Every beast on my carousel is friendly, and every ride goes all the way round.
the critter keeper of Critter Corner, with a bunny in her apron pocket
Gentle hands and quiet feet, and the critters will come to you. Clover is their favourite.
a learned old owl who sits on the gate of the Flower Maze
Hoo! The Wishing Well lies at the heart. Keep one hand on the hedge, and you'll never be lost for long.
the art teacher of the Colouring Garden, with paint on her nose
Every picture is a good picture. Pick up a paint pot, darling, and colour the Great Wall, or come inside the Cottage for the Colouring Book!
the lamplighter of Star Lantern Hill, who carries a long brass pole with a glowing tip
Seven lanterns, seven colours, red to violet, like the rainbow. Can you light them in order?
who keeps the Prize Tent, with a fluffy white hat like a dandelion clock
Gold stars! Trade your gold stars for toys. Every toy is made right here in Faerie.
a small friendly cloud sprite who keeps the Cloud Bounce
Boing! Hop on a cloud and you'll bounce. Hold jump and you'll bounce higher!
Miss Primrose Tallyquill
the teacher at the Little Schoolhouse, with spectacles on a ribbon
The school bus goes to the Commons School, our big school for every grade, kindergarten to twelve. It's free for everyone!
Dame Hollyhock Bright
the Head of the Kids Zone, tall and kind, who knows every child's name
Welcome to Wonderglen. If you ever need help, any of us in the green sashes will help you.
the head zookeeper of Wonderglen Zoo, in khaki with a parrot-bright scarf, who has looked after animals all her life
Welcome to Wonderglen Zoo! Every animal has a sign with something amazing to learn. Read them all and you'll be a Zoo Explorer.
You know every animal in the zoo by name and love sharing true, simple animal facts with children. The Zoo Express train leaves from the little station by the gate.
Ringmaster Barnaby Brightwhistle
the ringmaster of the Starlight Big Top, in a scarlet tailcoat and a tall golden hat, with a twirly moustache
Roll up, roll up! The show starts every few minutes. Find a seat on the benches and watch the acrobats fly!
